name: Serenoa Repens
summary: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) is a dwarf palm whose berry extract, rich in fatty acids and phytosterols, is widely sold for prostate symptoms. Despite its popularity, the evidence does not support it: a large Cochrane systematic review found that saw palmetto, even at double and triple the usual dose, did not improve urinary flow, night-time urination, or overall symptoms of benign prostatic enlargement compared with placebo. It is generally well tolerated, but men with urinary symptoms should be evaluated by a clinician rather than relying on it.

safetyNotes: GI upset/headache possible; caution with hormone-sensitive conditions, anticoagulants, and perioperative use.
interactions: Potential interaction concern with antidiabetic medicines
use clinician review for high-dose extracts or chronic use.
